outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no perfect cuboid has been found and no accepted resolution of the existence question has appeared. The in-window activity is (a) a 2026 cluster of unrefereed claims of full nonexistence (Yelle, Liu, Muhammad, Reed), none of them checked publicly by anyone qualified; (b) a bounded-fiber exclusion of perfect cuboids on 1,072 explicit master-tuple fibers with max(m,n) at most 100 (Peschmann, April 2026), extended to all 2,040 admissible fibers with m at most 100 by Cipollini (September 2026), whose paper credits GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra with the remaining arguments and the computational package; and (c) partial results on the associated cuboid conjectures (Asiryan, 2025-2026), which by Wikipedia's own account would imply nonexistence only if all three conjectures held.
problem_asks: Read from the statement and the Wikipedia link target, unpacked into parts. Part 1 (existence): does there exist a perfect cuboid, a rectangular box whose three edges, three face diagonals and space diagonal are all positive integers, i.e. a positive-integer solution of a^2+b^2=d^2, b^2+c^2=e^2, a^2+c^2=f^2, a^2+b^2+c^2=g^2 (a perfect Euler brick). Part 2 (associated cuboid conjectures): the bullet names no conjecture itself. Its link goes to Wikipedia's Cuboid conjectures article, which names three, and I take these as the associated conjectures. Cuboid conjecture 1: for coprime positive integers a not equal to u, the degree-8 polynomial P_{a,u}(t) is irreducible over the integers. Cuboid conjecture 2: for coprime positive integers p not equal to q, the degree-10 polynomial Q_{p,q}(t) is irreducible over the integers. Cuboid conjecture 3: for coprime positive integers a, b, u avoiding six listed equality cases, the degree-12 polynomial P_{a,b,u}(t) is irreducible over the integers. The Wikipedia article says these three are neither proved nor disproved and are not equivalent to the perfect cuboid question, but that if all three are true then no perfect cuboid exists. The statement does not say what is asked of the conjectures (proof, or only their relation to existence); I have recorded all three as parts. Part 1 also has a second formulation in the literature, the Cuboid Conjecture 'no perfect cuboid exists in N^3' (Peschmann arXiv:2604.28072, Conjecture 1.1), which is the same question as Part 1.

events.what_happened: Sawyer and Reiter, 'Perfect parallelepipeds exist' (arXiv:0907.0220; Mathematics of Computation 2011). Exhibits non-rectangular parallelepipeds whose edges, face diagonals and body diagonal are all integers (example edges 271, 106, 103). Discarded: it is not a rectangular box, so it is not a perfect cuboid. Not opened; described in the Wikipedia Perfect cuboid article (opened) and a search-result abstract (not opened).
events.revisions: Published Mathematics of Computation 80 (2011), per search results and Wikipedia.
events.delivers: Integer-edged, integer-diagonal parallelepipeds (non-rectangular) exist. Says nothing about rectangular boxes.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the object found is not a cuboid.

checked_by.what_they_did: published the paper in 2011 (per search results; not opened)

events.direction: Not about the problem: a different object (non-rectangular parallelepiped).
events.object: A non-rectangular parallelepiped with all edges, face diagonals and body diagonal integral (edges 271, 106, 103). Exhibited explicitly. It does not satisfy the rectangularity that the perfect cuboid requires.

events.what_happened: Sharipov, 'Perfect cuboids and irreducible polynomials' (arXiv:1108.5348; ID implies August 2011). Reduces the perfect cuboid problem to a family of univariate polynomials and conjectures their irreducibility over the integers; the search summary says irreducibility would imply nonexistence and that the conjecture was checked numerically for about 10,000 parameter instances. Not opened; the source is a search summary only. This is the origin of the associated cuboid conjectures named in the statement.
events.delivers: A conjecture-proposing reduction: if the cuboid polynomials are irreducible under the stated restrictions, no perfect cuboid exists. No irreducibility proved here.
events.remains: Parts 1 and 2 of problem_asks, all three cuboid conjectures.
events.doubts: Conjectural only (per the search summary). Not read directly.
events.direction: Proposes conjectures which, if true, imply that no perfect cuboid exists. Does not assert nonexistence.

events.what_happened: Drushinin (also spelled Druzhinin) and Lazarev, 'The proof of the impossibility of the existence of perfect cuboid', European Science Review, 2014 (Sarov Physico-Technical Institute, MEPHI). Claims a proof of impossibility using a quadratic identity for building Pythagorean chains. Opened only the CyberLeninka abstract page (Russian-language aggregator); the full article was not opened.
events.delivers: Claims full nonexistence of an integer brick with all seven values integral (per abstract). Nothing about the argument's steps is visible to me.
events.remains: None, if the claim holds; not checked.
events.doubts: The aggregator page does not state a peer-review process or an issue. No independent discussion found. The claim has not been checked by me.
events.direction: Claims the perfect cuboid does not exist.

events.what_happened: Wyss, 'No Perfect Cuboid' (arXiv:1506.02215, math.NT), first posted 7 June 2015; abstract: 'We prove that there is no perfect cuboid.' Five versions to 17 May 2017 (v2 27 Jun 2015, v3 12 Jun 2016, v4 14 Jun 2016, v5 17 May 2017). No journal reference, no withdrawal notice on the abstract page. Sharipov's 2017 check (separate event) examined version 4 and found a specific error.
events.revisions: v2 27 Jun 2015; v3 12 Jun 2016; v4 14 Jun 2016; v5 17 May 2017 (current on abstract page). Not opened in full; whether v5 changes the argument was not established.
events.delivers: Claims full nonexistence of a perfect cuboid (abstract claim).

checked_by.qualification: author of arXiv papers on the cuboid polynomials (search summaries list arXiv:1108.5348 and a 2018 survey in Itogi Nauki i Tekhniki)
checked_by.what_they_did: Found a specific error in version 4 (see sharipov-2017-wyss-check). Did not confirm or refute the final claim for later versions.

events.doubts: A specific error in the rectangular case was identified in version 4 by Sharipov (2017): Wyss takes a limit D to 0 and treats r and r1 as equal, where Sharipov says infinitesimally equal does not mean equal. Whether versions 5 (May 2017) repair this was not checked. No later verification found.
events.direction: Claims nonexistence, which would answer Part 1 in the negative.

events.what_happened: Computer search by Robert Matson, cited by Wikipedia as Matson 2015 (unsolvedproblems.org) for the bound: if a perfect cuboid exists its odd edge exceeds 2.5 x 10^13, and its smallest edge exceeds 5 x 10^11. Secondary sources also mention a 2013 blog-posted bound (odd side below 5 trillion) and a 2022 report (odd side below 25 trillion; minimum side below 500 billion). The unsolvedproblems.org report was not opened.
events.revisions: A 2022 update (odd side below 25 trillion) is reported by secondary sources, date not verified. The 2013 figure is a blog post.
events.delivers: Finite search: no perfect cuboid below stated size thresholds. Does not settle existence (a larger example is not excluded).
events.directly_checkable: Exhaustive search over Pythagorean-triple partners, described in secondary sources; not reproduced.
events.doubts: Computational bounds only. The Wikipedia-cited conclusion that the trend does not favour existence is contested in a forum post as too strong for the number of cases checked (search summary).
events.direction: Does not assert or refute existence; excludes small examples.

events.what_happened: Plick, 'A New Constraint on Perfect Cuboids', INTEGERS 17 (2017), A3 (received 10/5/14, accepted 1/23/17, published 2/13/17 per the journal index in search results). Constraint: among the seven segment lengths (three edges, three face diagonals, space diagonal) at least one is divisible by 25; among the other six, either one is divisible by 25 or two by 5. Abstract text is from a search result; the EMIS PDF returned HTTP 503 and was not opened.
events.delivers: A necessary divisibility constraint on any perfect cuboid. Not a construction; no existence or nonexistence claim.

checked_by.what_they_did: accepted and published the paper, per journal index in search results

events.direction: Necessary condition; neither proves nor disproves existence.

events.what_happened: Belogourov, 2019, cited by Wikipedia for the bound: if a perfect cuboid exists its space diagonal exceeds 9 x 10^15. Exhaustive search of edge and face cuboids (Wikipedia says as of December 2017 the search counted edge and face cuboids with space diagonal below about 1.1 x 10^15). Source not opened.
events.delivers: Finite search bound on the space diagonal of a hypothetical perfect cuboid. Does not settle existence.
events.doubts: Computational bound, not reproduced.
events.direction: Excludes small space diagonals; does not assert or refute existence.

events.direction: Does not bear on existence of a perfect cuboid; it counts non-perfect cuboids.

events.what_happened: Lloyd, 'There is no Perfect Cuboid' (arXiv:2206.06160). v1 8 June 2022; v2 16 July 2022, withdrawn; v3 12 January 2024, comment 'Revised solution'. Main claim: 'This simple proof shows that the internal diagonal of an Euler brick cannot be an odd integer.' Since a perfect cuboid must have an odd internal diagonal (a parity fact Wikipedia lists), this would exclude perfect cuboids. Abstract page opened; the argument's odd-diagonal step was not read.
events.revisions: v2 16 Jul 2022 (withdrawn); v3 12 Jan 2024 ('Revised solution'), which is the current text. The v3 revision date is before the frozen revision.
events.delivers: If correct: no Euler brick has an odd internal diagonal, hence no perfect cuboid (the parity premise is cited as known). Scope: whole problem as stated, via a parity argument.
events.remains: Nothing, if the argument holds; the cuboid conjectures are not addressed.
events.doubts: No critique or journal publication found. The argument was not checked by me. The v2 withdrawal (July 2022) has no stated reason, and the v3 'Revised solution' comment does not say what changed.

events.what_happened: Maiti, 'Multiple and Complete New Important Conjectures on Perfect Cuboid and Euler Brick' (arXiv:2312.09091), first posted 14 December 2023 under an earlier title on Pythagorean triples and biquadratic equations. Proposes 12 conjectures; claims that any perfect cuboid, if one exists, must be among the solutions of six conjectures and all primitive Euler bricks among three more. Says nobody has discovered a perfect cuboid. Nothing is proved here.
events.revisions: v2 20 Dec 2023; v3 23 Dec 2023; v4 17 Jan 2024; v5 1 Feb 2024 (titles change across versions, per search results); v6 6 Apr 2026; v7 16 Apr 2026. Abstract page opened (version history read there); full text not read.
events.delivers: Conjectures only: a reduction of the perfect cuboid question to six conjectures, if any perfect cuboid exists. No resolution of any part.
events.doubts: Conjectures, unproved, and the author's later versions (2026) keep them conjectural. No independent discussion found.
events.direction: Neutral: proposes conjectures which would describe any perfect cuboid; does not assert existence or nonexistence.

events.what_happened: de Grey, Gibbs and Helm, 'Novel required properties of, and efficient algorithms to seek, perfect cuboids' (arXiv:2401.06784, math.GM), submitted 6 January 2024; journal reference Geombinatorics Quarterly XXXIII(3), 2024. Claims two new computer search algorithms (derived from perfect plinths) that are much more efficient than prior ones; identifies new two-parameter families of edge cuboids; shows large proportions of face and internal-rectangle aspect ratios cannot occur in a perfect cuboid (previously known only for 4:3). No existence result and, per the paper as read, no explicit lower bound. Abstract page opened.
events.revisions: Only v1 listed. Journal reference Geombinatorics Quarterly 2024.
events.delivers: Restrictions on the aspect ratios of faces and internal rectangles of any perfect cuboid (large proportions excluded), plus search algorithms. Does not settle existence.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: existence is untouched; the cuboid conjectures are untouched.

checked_by.qualification: journal of record for the paper
checked_by.what_they_did: published the paper (journal reference on the arXiv page); refereeing not verified

events.directly_checkable: Aspect-ratio restrictions and search algorithms: checkable from the paper; not reproduced.
events.direction: Partial: restricts the shape of any perfect cuboid; does not move existence.

events.what_happened: Riley Tao (not Terence Tao), 'Nonexistence of Euler Boxes with Semiprime Sides' (arXiv:2401.05276, math.NT), first posted 10 January 2024; one version; 9 pages. Main theorem: 'No Euler boxes exist with a semiprime side length.' The abstract says 'there cannot exist a perfect Euler box with a semiprime side'. The introduction states a perfect Euler box has all sides, face diagonals and space diagonal integral; its treatment of Euler box is garbled. A search summary says the paper was written in October 2021; that date is not on the arXiv page and was not verified. Abstract and HTML v1 opened.
events.revisions: None (single version, v1). Write-up date (October 2021) per a search summary only.
events.delivers: No side of a perfect cuboid (or of an Euler box, if the theorem's wording is taken literally) is a semiprime. A restricted case: one side of the box, under a semiprime condition.
events.remains: Every other side and all other cases of Part 1 and Part 2.
events.directly_checkable: Elementary number theory per the paper; not checked.
events.doubts: Scope ambiguity: the theorem says 'Euler boxes' and the abstract says 'perfect Euler box'. If Euler boxes are meant (space diagonal not required integral), the result is broader than the perfect cuboid question; if perfect boxes are meant, it is a restricted case. The paper notes earlier results (Kor92: the space diagonal of a perfect Euler box is not semiprime). Not checked by experts.
events.direction: Partial: excludes a special class of sides; does not assert or refute existence.

events.what_happened: Taha Muhammad, 'Euler Perfect Box' (Cambridge Open Engage working paper series). First posted 29 May 2024 (Version 1). Versions in the Cambridge series per search results and the pages read: 8 Aug 2024; 30 Sep 2024; 16 Dec 2024 ('3rd Way'); 20 Dec 2024 ('2nd Way'); 1 Jun 2025 ('2nd Way'); 10 Jun 2025 ('Final', opened); 12 May 2026 ('2nd Way' v1); 20 May 2026 ('2nd Way' v2); the 'Version 4' page is dated 17 May 2026. Each claims no Euler perfect box exists. The 2024 v1 argues by cases on the edge lengths (a, a+r, a+k; two equal edges make the space diagonal non-integral); the 2025 Final abstract reads 'I have to prove that g in N+' before concluding that the Euler Perfect Box does not exist. Pages opened: v1 (29 May 2024) and Final (10 Jun 2025). Later versions not opened.
events.revisions: Many versions; see what_happened. The argument changes structure across versions (three 'ways', then 'Final').
events.delivers: Claims full nonexistence of a perfect box (all sides, face diagonals and space diagonal integral), by a case split on the edge lengths.
events.doubts: Self-posted; the Cambridge page says it is not peer-reviewed by Cambridge University Press. The Final abstract excerpt reads 'I have to prove that g in N+', which the author states as a remaining step. A comment on one page by the author says a journal (Mitteilungen Klosterneuburg) found the paper suitable for publication; no journal record found, and the comment is the author's own. Cambridge metrics on the Final page: 397 views, 62 downloads, 0 citations at snapshot. Not checked by anyone qualified.
events.direction: Claims the perfect cuboid does not exist.

events.what_happened: Valery Asiryan, 'On the Irreducibility of the Cuboid Polynomial P_{a,u}(t)' (arXiv:2510.07643, math.GM), first posted 9 October 2025, v2 12 October 2025. Claims P_{a,u}(t) (even monic, degree 8, integer parameters) admits no nontrivial factorization in Z[t], by excluding 4+4, 2+6 and other splittings. The abstract does not name Cuboid conjecture 1; the polynomial is Sharipov's first cuboid polynomial per the companion paper's comments and introduction. Abstract page opened.
events.revisions: v2 12 Oct 2025 (current).
events.delivers: Irreducibility over Z of P_{a,u}(t) for the parameter range the abstract states (a, u with the restrictions of the paper). If the claim holds, this covers Cuboid conjecture 1 in the cuboid setting. It says nothing about perfect cuboids directly; by Wikipedia's account, the conjecture alone does not settle existence.
events.remains: Cuboid conjectures 2 and 3; existence (Part 1), which Wikipedia says needs all three conjectures.
events.directly_checkable: Factorization exclusions by 2- and 3-adic analysis and a discriminant argument, per the abstract; not checked.
events.doubts: Single author, no journal, no engagement found. The paper does not state a consequence for perfect cuboids. Full text not read.
events.direction: Proves the associated irreducibility claim (Cuboid conjecture 1 in its setting). Does not assert or refute existence.

events.what_happened: Valery Asiryan, 'Irreducibility of the Cuboid Polynomial P_{a,u}(t) via a Rank-Zero Elliptic Curve' (arXiv:2510.11768, math.GM). v1 13 Oct 2025; v2 6 Feb 2026; v3 15 Mar 2026. Comment field on v3: 'A complete short proof of the first perfect cuboid conjecture (Sharipov's first conjecture)'. Abstract: 'For nonzero integers a,u with u^2 != a^2 we prove that P_{a,u}(t) is irreducible in Z[t]'. Theorem 1 (v3): 'For any integers a,u with au != 0 and u^2 != a^2, the polynomial P_{a,u}(t) in Z[t] is irreducible.' The introduction states the cuboid setting as a,u positive, gcd(a,u)=1, a != u. The v1 abstract relied on a Magma rank/torsion computation (search summary; v1 not opened). Abstract and theorem read from v3 HTML.
events.revisions: v2 6 Feb 2026; v3 15 Mar 2026 (current). Hypotheses are broader in v3 than the cuboid setting; the summary says v1 used a Magma computation.
events.delivers: Irreducibility of P_{a,u}(t) over Z for all integers with au nonzero and u^2 different from a^2 (v3). This contains the cuboid setting of Cuboid conjecture 1, and so would confirm it if correct. It says nothing about perfect cuboids directly.
events.directly_checkable: Computation via a rank-zero elliptic curve (rank and torsion); the v1 computation was in Magma per the search summary.
events.doubts: Scope drift: the theorem's hypotheses (all integers, u^2 != a^2) are wider than the conjecture's (positive coprime a != u). Whether the author intends the wider statement is not clear. The comment calls it a complete proof; no independent check found. The author-supplied comment is the only statement connecting it to the perfect cuboid conjecture.
events.direction: Proves the associated irreducibility claim, in a broader hypothesis range than the conjecture. Does not assert or refute existence.

events.what_happened: Valery Asiryan, 'Non-Existence of Linear-Quartic Factorization for the Second Cuboid Quintic' (arXiv:2601.04241), first posted 5 January 2026, v2 12 January 2026. Shows that for rational s > 0, s not 1, the normalized quintic P_s has no rational roots, so Q_{p,q} has no linear factor over Q or Z; authors describe it as partial progress on Sharipov's second conjecture. Uses Magma and Chabauty's method (computer-assisted). Abstract page opened.
events.revisions: v2 12 Jan 2026 (current).
events.delivers: Cuboid conjecture 2 is only partly addressed: only the 1+4 (linear) factorization case is excluded.
events.remains: Cuboid conjecture 2 in all other factorization patterns; Cuboid conjecture 3; existence.
events.directly_checkable: Computer-assisted (Magma; Chabauty on a genus-2 curve), per the abstract; not reproduced.
events.doubts: Partial by its own description. Computer-assisted with no independent check found. Does not address perfect cuboids.
events.direction: Partial: one factorization case of Cuboid conjecture 2.

events.what_happened: Valery Asiryan and Randall L. Rathbun, 'Computational Evidence Against Quadratic-Cubic Factorization for the Second Cuboid Quintic' (arXiv:2601.07899), first posted 12 January 2026, v2 22 January 2026. Height-bounded search (H = 10^9) for rational points, giving computational evidence against a 2+3 factorization of the normalized quintic for rational s > 0, s not 1, conditional on completeness of the enumeration on the curve (named in the abstract). s = 1 is not ruled out. Magma named as the only software. Abstract page opened.
events.revisions: v2 22 Jan 2026 (current).
events.delivers: Computational evidence, conditional on enumeration completeness, against one factorization pattern (2+3) of the second cuboid quintic. Not a proof.
events.remains: Cuboid conjecture 2 in its other patterns; s = 1; Cuboid conjecture 3; existence.
events.directly_checkable: Height-bounded search; the abstract states the bound and the conditionality.
events.doubts: Explicitly conditional on completeness of the rational-point enumeration, and height-bounded. Not a proof.
events.direction: Partial and computational: evidence against one factorization of Cuboid conjecture 2's polynomial.

events.what_happened: Stephane Yelle, 'An Elementary Obstruction to the Existence of a Perfect Cuboid' (arXiv:2602.00239, math.GM). v1 posted 30 January 2026 with the claim 'This method provides an elementary proof of the non-existence of a perfect cuboid', by infinite descent along the space diagonal using a minimal odd prime in the triangular remainders. v2 posted 9 February 2026. v2 abstract still reads 'This approach provides an elementary obstruction to the existence of a perfect cuboid', but its introduction says 'The purpose of this paper is not to claim a definitive impossibility result', and its conclusion says 'The present analysis does not claim to resolve the existence problem for a perfect cuboid.' Both HTML versions opened; v1 claim quoted from the v1 HTML.
events.revisions: v2 9 Feb 2026: the impossibility claim is disclaimed in the introduction and conclusion, while the v2 abstract still says 'elementary obstruction'. Not formally withdrawn.
events.delivers: v1: claims full nonexistence. v2: an exploratory framework; none of the constructions it examines yields a non-degenerate Euler cuboid; no claim of nonexistence.
events.remains: v2: all of problem_asks. v1 (if its claim held): none.
events.doubts: The author's own v2 text retracts the impossibility claim in substance (the introduction and conclusion disclaim it), while the v2 abstract still speaks of an 'obstruction'. v1's proof was not checked by me, and no reviewer or critic has been found. The v2 abstract and body disagree.
events.direction: v1 claims nonexistence; v2 disclaims a definitive impossibility result.

events.what_happened: Zenodo record 18649401: 'A Complete Proof of the Non-Existence of Perfect Cuboids Based on Differential Algebraic Closure and Finite Representation Theory of Transcendental Functions'. Published 15 February 2026 (record says submitted 31 December 2025); version 1; preprint; CC BY 4.0; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18649401; affiliation Peking University. Claims 'rigorously prove that there does not exist a rectangular parallelepiped (perfect cuboid)'. Method (per the record abstract): reduce to a single-variable octic in the square of the edge ratio, build a differential algebraic closure, then 2-adic valuation arguments on congruences mod 8 for a contradiction. Record page opened; full PDF not opened.
events.revisions: None found (version 1).
events.delivers: Claims full nonexistence of a perfect cuboid (abstract claim).
events.doubts: Authorship unclear: the record metadata lists 'liu, shifa' as rights holder, not necessarily author. The Peking University affiliation is taken from the record. The abstract reportedly says it corrects a framework from earlier work (search summary, not confirmed). No expert engagement or journal record found; the record states no peer review. Full text not read.
events.direction: Claims the perfect cuboid does not exist.
people: Shifa Liu (listed on the record; authorship to be confirmed)

events.what_happened: Jonathan Reed, 'Proof of the Non-existence of Perfect Cuboids via Mordell-Weil Rank Exhaustion and Minimal Polynomial Irreducibility of the Perfect Cuboid Surface'. Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18948631 (version 1.0, published 11 March 2026) and DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19074228 (version 2; publication date 11 March 2026; created 17 March 2026; modified 16 September 2026). Author ORCID on record: 0009-0008-7345-1407. Abstract: 'This manuscript establishes the non-existence of the Perfect Cuboid.' Reduces the problem to rational points on genus-3 hyperelliptic curves and claims their Jacobians have Mordell-Weil rank zero. The Zenodo abstract adds that non-existence of rational solutions is 'further verified via formal methods in Lean 4'. GitHub repository AEjonanonymous/Non-existence-of-Perfect-Cuboids (36 commits, 1 star; last updated 7 October 2026) holds NoPerfectCuboids.lean (Lean; mathlib-stable per Lean Web and Comparator links) and the 'Formal Proof' PDF. Re-deposit on Hexagon as hexagon:2610.00137v1, 7 October 2026 (see the AI field), with the same title and abstract. The first public written argument is dated to the March Zenodo version because the same mathematics was first posted then.
events.revisions: Zenodo 18948631 v1.0 (11 Mar 2026); Zenodo 19074228 v2 (publication date shown 11 Mar 2026; newer versions exist per the page); Hexagon hexagon:2610.00137v1 (7 Oct 2026), which adds the AI acknowledgement quoted below. Hexagon page does not state whether it differs in mathematics from the March version. Not compared.
events.delivers: Claims full nonexistence (abstract claim). In the Lean file, the main theorem no_perfect_cuboid_final concludes False from two hypotheses: h_rational_limit (is_torsion_point u, i.e. u is 0, 1 or -1) and h_perfection_req (phi_perfection u = 0). Per a summarising fetch of the raw file, neither hypothesis is derived in the file; the file proves only that the torsion candidates fail the perfection equation. A separate lemma (parity_wall_consistency) proves a mod-8 contradiction for one residue assignment (x^2 = 4, y^2 = 0, z^2 = 1 mod 8). The formal file therefore does not establish nonexistence on its own.
events.remains: If the paper's argument is accepted, nothing; as the Lean file stands, the rational-limit step and the perfection equation are assumptions, so the formal result is conditional.

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 (Mathlib, stable, per Lean Web and Comparator links)

events.directly_checkable: Lean file NoPerfectCuboids.lean and two Python scripts (Saunderson_P_Lift_calculator.py, Saunderson_parametric_sweep.py) in the repository. Read only through a summarising fetch; sorry-free status is from that summary (keyword count zero), not a raw read.
events.doubts: (1) The main Lean theorem assumes its two key hypotheses (u torsion; phi_perfection u = 0). Per the fetched summary of the file, neither is derived there, so the formal result is conditional on them. (2) The mod-8 lemma covers one residue case. (3) The Zenodo abstract's claim that the non-existence of rational solutions is 'verified via formal methods in Lean 4' should be read against (1). (4) The paper's Mordell-Weil rank-zero claim is not checked. (5) No peer review, no expert engagement, no institutional affiliation found on the Zenodo or Hexagon pages. (6) The Hexagon page labels the work 'A mix of human-written and AI-generated text'.
events.direction: Claims the perfect cuboid does not exist.

events.what_happened: René Peschmann, 'Quartic reductions and elliptic obstructions for perfect Euler bricks' (arXiv:2604.09328), single author, first posted 10 April 2026, one version. Reduces the problem to a pair of simultaneous-square quartic conditions, relates them to genus-3 hyperelliptic curves, and derives obstructions on an elliptic quotient; reports computational checks for parameters up to 10^3. Explicitly does not claim nonexistence: 'These results do not yet exclude perfect Euler bricks unconditionally.' Abstract page opened.
events.revisions: None (v1 only).
events.delivers: Framework and unconditional obstructions on the elliptic quotient; computational checks up to 10^3. Does not exclude perfect Euler bricks in general.
events.doubts: Computational checks up to 10^3 only; its own conclusion is partial.
events.direction: Partial: obstructions, no nonexistence claim.

events.what_happened: René Peschmann, 'A torsion-intersection proof of perfect-cuboid nonexistence on 1,072 explicit master-tuple fibers' (arXiv:2604.28072; math.NT, math.AG; companion to 2604.09328), single author, submitted 30 April 2026, one version. Claims an unconditional proof of the Cuboid Conjecture (Conjecture 1.1: no perfect cuboid exists in N^3, 'Conjecture B') on 1,072 explicit master-tuple fibers with max(m,n) at most 100. Theorem 1.3: if one elliptic quotient has rank zero and the lift count equals 8, then all rational points are degenerate and no perfect cuboid lies on that (m,n)-fiber. Rank-zero certificates use PARI/GP ellrank and Sage exact L(E,1)/Omega evaluation, with the modularity theorem, Kolyvagin's theorem and Edixhoven's bound on the Manin constant. The author states the result is unconditional on the 1,072 fibers. It is not a proof for all fibers, and the paper says so (per Cipollini's paper). A GitHub repository renpe/euler-brick-obstructions is mentioned in the PDF metadata; not opened. Abstract page and HTML v1 opened; the PDF was unreadable.
events.revisions: None (v1 only).
events.delivers: Nonexistence of perfect cuboids on the 1,072 explicit master-tuple fibers with max(m,n) at most 100 (fiber-by-fiber). Not the global Cuboid Conjecture.
events.remains: Nonexistence on the other fibers (all (m,n) not among the 1,072), i.e. the global Conjecture 1.1; existence in general (Part 1).
events.directly_checkable: Rank-zero certificates by PARI/GP ellrank and Sage L-value evaluation (per abstract). Code linked to a GitHub repository (not opened).
events.doubts: Unconditional claim rests on rank-zero computations and on the lift-count condition; not checked by anyone qualified publicly. The later Cipollini paper builds directly on it (use, not verification). A rank-zero certificate that uses modularity, Kolyvagin and Edixhoven is a long chain of cited results; each is standard but the combination is unrefereed.
events.direction: Claims nonexistence of perfect cuboids on a bounded set of fibers (1,072 explicit fibers with max(m,n) at most 100).

events.what_happened: René Peschmann, 'Exponent-one blockers and a Mordell-Weil construction of Euler bricks' (arXiv:2605.00573), single author, first posted 1 May 2026, one version. Computational observation: for every coprime-Pythagorean-pair parametrisation the space-diagonal norm has a prime factor of exponent one avoiding 29 listed expressions, checked on 151,575 cases. Generates about 1.28 million Master-Hits via Mordell-Weil combinations; 'None of the resulting 1,284,670 Master-Hits is a perfect cuboid.' Explicitly not a proof. Abstract page opened.
events.revisions: None (v1 only).
events.delivers: A computational observation and a generator of Euler bricks, none of which is a perfect cuboid. No proof of nonexistence.
events.directly_checkable: Exact integer arithmetic on the generated cases (per abstract).
events.doubts: Empirical; not a theorem.
events.direction: Neither: empirical finding that generated bricks are not perfect cuboids.

events.what_happened: Ricky Cipollini, 'Elimination of Rene Peschmann's 968 Remaining Hard Fibers for the Perfect Cuboid Problem' (arXiv:2609.14526, math.NT), single author, submitted 13 September 2026, v1 only. Eliminates the 968 fibers (of 2,040 admissible coprime pairs with max(m,n) at most 100) left open by Peschmann's 1,072, so with Peschmann's result no perfect cuboid exists on any of the 2,040 fibers with m at most 100 (Corollary 3). Theorem 2: no positive master-tuple specialisation (a,b,m,n) gives a perfect cuboid for these (m,n). Most fibers fall to short rank-zero or covering arguments; the last cases need stronger local-global sieves. The paper says it is 'still a bounded-fiber theorem rather than a proof of the full perfect-cuboid conjecture' and that Corollary 3 'is not the global perfect-cuboid conjecture'. Its acknowledgements credit AI models with LaTeX/polishing and with the remaining arguments and the computational package (see the AI field). Read from arXiv HTML v1 via a summarising fetch; the PDF was unreadable. Quotes below are from that fetch and from matching search-result text.
events.revisions: None (v1 only).
events.delivers: Nonexistence of perfect cuboids on the 968 remaining fibers (Theorem 2 and Corollary 3). Combined with Peschmann's 1,072, perfect cuboids are excluded on all 2,040 admissible fibers with m at most 100. Explicitly restricted to these bounded fibers; not the global Cuboid Conjecture.
events.remains: Nonexistence on fibers with m above 100 (the global Conjecture 1.1); existence in general (Part 1); all of Part 2 (cuboid conjectures 1-3 not addressed).
events.directly_checkable: Computational package at github.com/mrricky22/968-fibers (repository holds '968_fiber_package.zip'; repository page has no README; the zip not opened). Per the paper, the package contains the exact inputs, scripts, outputs and fiber-by-fiber data. Not formal (no Lean/Coq).
events.doubts: Restricted to bounded fibers (max(m,n) at most 100); the author says so. The computational package was created by an AI model (GPT-6 Astra, per the author), and the remaining arguments for 968 fibers come from AI models (per the author). The author states the core 585-fiber argument is their own. No independent check of the package or of the arguments is public. The paper uses the Peschmann result as a base (Peschmann's paper is itself unrefereed).
events.direction: Claims nonexistence of perfect cuboids on a bounded set of fibers (all 2,040 admissible fibers with m at most 100 once combined with Peschmann's result).

events.what_happened: Two Wolfram Community posts by Ricky Cespedes on primitive Euler bricks: 'Branch-Switch Shared-Prime Congruence and Modular Obstruction Patterns in Primitive Euler Bricks', and 'A Branch-Switch Obstruction Phenomenon in Primitive Euler Bricks: Computational Through 1 Billion' (search-result text: search to 1.01 x 10^9; 1,968 primitive Euler bricks; 234 branch-switch candidates; 78 valid branch-switch pairs; 94 shared obstruction-prime events; 'no claim is made that the perfect cuboid problem is solved'). disputes.summary: At least nine published or posted claims of full nonexistence have appeared since 2014 (Drushinin and Lazarev 2014; Wyss 2015; Maiti 2020; Aleshkevich 2022; Lloyd 2022; Yelle v1 January 2026; Liu February 2026; Muhammad 2024-2026; Reed March 2026). None has been accepted by anyone qualified in the sources I read. Sharipov (2017) found a specific error in Wyss's version 4 that the later versions may or may not address; that dispute is unresolved in the record.

Asiryan's 2025 paper 2510.11768 (v3) states the irreducibility of P_{a,u}(t) for all integers with au nonzero and u^2 different from a^2. Wikipedia's Cuboid conjecture 1 is for coprime positive a different from u. The paper's introduction states the narrower cuboid setting. The wider theorem is a different hypothesis set, and the paper's comment calls it a 'complete short proof of the first perfect cuboid conjecture'.

Yelle arXiv:2602.00239: v1 claims an elementary proof of nonexistence; v2 introduction and conclusion disclaim a definitive impossibility result, but the v2 abstract still says 'This approach provides an elementary obstruction to the existence of a perfect cuboid'.

Riley Tao's arXiv:2401.05276: the theorem reads 'No Euler boxes exist with a semiprime side length' while the abstract reads 'a perfect Euler box with a semiprime side'. Whether the theorem covers non-perfect Euler boxes is not settled by the text I read.
Zenodo 18649401 names Shifa Liu as rights holder ('liu, shifa'), and the search summary attributes the paper to Liu. Whether Liu is the author is not confirmed.

Lean formalisation and mathematical claim disagree in strength: the Zenodo abstract says non-existence is 'verified via formal methods in Lean 4', but the Lean main theorem takes its two key hypotheses (u is torsion; phi_perfection u = 0) as assumptions (per the summary of the raw file).

summary: Fifty-five web searches and about forty-five fetches, with every primary source opened that I could reach, found no resolution of the perfect cuboid question and no accepted nonexistence proof. Since 26 January 2024 the activity is: (a) Peschmann's arXiv:2604.28072 (30 April 2026), claiming an unconditional nonexistence proof on 1,072 explicit master-tuple fibers with max(m,n) at most 100, with a companion (2604.09328) that disclaims a full proof and a computational paper (2605.00573) that finds no perfect cuboid among 1,284,670 generated bricks; (b) Cipollini's arXiv:2609.14526 (13 September 2026), which eliminates the remaining 968 fibers, so that with Peschmann's result perfect cuboids are excluded on all 2,040 admissible fibers with m at most 100. The paper calls itself a bounded-fiber theorem. Its acknowledgements, as the author words them, credit GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra with the remaining arguments and GPT-6 Astra with the computational package; the core 585-fiber argument is the author's. This is the only AI attribution I found that is load-bearing on this problem in a source; the quotes were read through a summarising fetch because the PDF was unreadable, so they should be checked against the raw HTML. (c) Unrefereed full-nonexistence claims: Yelle (arXiv:2602.00239; v1 claims a proof, v2 disclaims a definitive impossibility result while its abstract still says 'obstruction'); Liu (Zenodo 18649401, 15 February 2026); Muhammad (Cambridge Engage, 29 May 2024 to May 2026, many versions, self-posted); and Reed (Zenodo 18948631 and 19074228, 11 March 2026; Lean repository AEjonanonymous/Non-existence-of-Perfect-Cuboids; a Hexagon re-deposit, hexagon:2610.00137v1, on 7 October 2026 that acknowledges Gemini 'for its role as a formalization and editing tool'). For Reed, the Lean main theorem no_perfect_cuboid_final takes is_torsion_point u and phi_perfection u = 0 as hypotheses, and per the summary of the raw file neither is derived, so the formal file does not by itself establish nonexistence. (d) Partial results on the associated cuboid conjectures (the three named on Wikipedia's Cuboid conjectures page): Asiryan's arXiv:2510.07643 and arXiv:2510.11768 (October 2025; v3 March 2026) claim irreducibility of P_{a,u}(t), i.e. Cuboid conjecture 1, with the v3 hypotheses broader than the conjecture's; Asiryan's arXiv:2601.04241 (January 2026) excludes only linear factors of Q_{p,q} (computer-assisted, Magma); Asiryan and Rathbun's arXiv:2601.07899 gives computational evidence, conditional on enumeration completeness, against a quadratic-cubic factorisation. Wikipedia says the three conjectures together would imply no perfect cuboid exists, so none of (d) settles Part 1. Pre-window items: Wyss (2015, Sharipov 2017 found a specific error in version 4: 'infinitesimally equal does not mean equal'); Maiti (2020); Aleshkevich (2022); Lloyd (2022, v3 January 2024, v2 withdrawn); Drushinin and Lazarev (2014, abstract only); Maiti's conjectures (December 2023, revised 2024 and 2026); de Grey, Gibbs and Helm (6 January 2024, aspect-ratio restrictions and search algorithms, published Geombinatorics Quarterly); and Riley Tao (10 January 2024, no side of a perfect box is semiprime, with a scope ambiguity between Euler boxes and perfect boxes). Riley Tao's posting precedes the 26 January 2024 freeze. Computer bounds (Matson 2015, Belogourov 2019, Rathbun 2020) exclude small examples only. AI search: beyond Cipollini and Reed, no AI attribution for this problem appeared; the OpenAI Astra ten-problem coverage (August 2026, secondary) does not mention a perfect cuboid; Epoch's FrontierMath open-problems page (updated 7 October 2026) has no perfect cuboid entry; the Open Problem Garden page's last comment is from 2012. Close calls: (i) whether bounded-fiber theorems settle any part of Part 1, given the author's own description; (ii) whether the AI roles in Cipollini are load-bearing, which the author's own sentence says they are for the remaining 968 fibers; (iii) whether Riley Tao's result is in-window (it is not, by a fortnight) and which class of boxes its theorem covers; (iv) whether Reed's AI acknowledgement applies to the March version of the claim, which the March Zenodo landing page does not mention, while the 7 October Hexagon version does.
competing_reading: Read strictly, the only substantive in-window progress on Part 1 is a computational exclusion on bounded fibers (Peschmann 2026, Cipollini 2026), and the judging pass may treat it as a restricted case that leaves existence open. Read more generously, Cipollini's paper, with its AI-written remaining arguments and package, is an unconditional exclusion of perfect cuboids on 2,040 fibers, and the AI involvement is load-bearing by the author's own sentence. Reed's Lean repository could be read as a full, machine-checked nonexistence result, but only if the assumed hypotheses of the main theorem are proved elsewhere, which the file, as summarised to me, does not do.
what_would_settle_it: A raw read of the arXiv PDFs of 2604.28072 and 2609.14526 (the quotes here come from summarising fetches), to confirm the acknowledgements word for word and the theorem scope. A referee report or journal decision on Peschmann and Cipollini. Independent rerun of the 968-fiber package. A raw read of NoPerfectCuboids.lean to confirm (1) whether is_torsion_point u and phi_perfection u = 0 are proved or assumed, and (2) the sorry-free status, followed by #print axioms. A statement from the Reed author and the Hexagon page on whether the March and October versions differ in mathematics and what Gemini produced. The Sharipov check of Wyss version 5 (May 2017). Whether Asiryan's cuboid-polynomial proofs hold, and whether the v3 hypotheses are the intended ones. Confirmation of Riley Tao's theorem scope (Euler box or perfect Euler box).
